Everyone acts like I’m supposed to just accept their version of it.\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?\n\nPatient: I don’t know… I mean, I get tired like anyone else. Sometimes I don’t sleep great when things are stressful, but “unusually energized” sounds kind of like one of those check-box phrases. I still have to get up for work, open the store, deal with everyone’s schedules, and then people act like if I’m alert it means something.\n\nSo… no, not that I’ve really noticed. I wouldn’t say I’m running around with extra energy or not needing sleep. It’s more just, you know, there’s a lot going on.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard voices when no one else was there?\n\nPatient: Voices? I mean… not like in the way people make it sound on TV, no. I don’t sit there hearing someone talking in an empty room or anything.\n\nSometimes I hear people talking nearby and I wonder if they’re talking about me, but that’s just because of the situation and how people have been acting. Like at work, when people lower their voices as I come around—anyone would notice that. But hearing voices when nobody is there? I don’t think so.\n\nDoctor: Have you found yourself feeling much less interested in being around other people than you used to?\n\nPatient: I don’t know if I’d say “less interested.” I mean, I’m around people all day at work, so it’s not like I’m living in a cave or something. Though honestly, after dealing with customers and staff and all the little side conversations, I sometimes just want to go home and have quiet.\n\nBut that’s normal, right? My sister does that too—she works at a salon and she says by the end of the day she doesn’t want anyone talking to her, not even the TV on loud. So I don’t know. It’s funny, because at work we had this whole safety training about ladders and falling boxes, and half the people weren’t even listening, which is exactly how accidents happen, but… no, I don’t think there was anything like that around when all this started.\n\nDoctor: Have you had a period when you felt deeply depressed most of the day nearly every day?\n\nPatient: I don’t know… “deeply depressed” sounds like a very specific thing. I guess I haven’t really been measuring it like that.\n\nDoctor: Have you believed that anyone was controlling your thoughts?\n\nPatient: Controlling my thoughts? No, not like putting thoughts in my head or anything like that.\n\nWhat I’ve been trying to explain is more… people keep acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork, like I missed some payments and that’s the whole story. But I know it’s not just that. The bank, the loan servicer, and even some people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And every time they show me another paper, it’s like they expect me to ignore what I’ve been seeing for almost two years.\n\nDoctor: Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts are hard to follow or seem jumbled?\n\nPatient: I don’t think people have said it like that, no. I don’t think that’s what’s happening. Sometimes I have to explain the background first, because if you don’t know all the pieces, then of course it sounds confusing. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Outside of the house… well, it doesn’t really stay outside the house, that’s the thing. People try to make it sound like it’s just foreclosure paperwork, late payments, forms, whatever, but it’s not just that.

The bank and the loan servicer have been working this in a way that’s too coordinated to be accidental. And then at work, certain people started acting differently too — like they knew things they shouldn’t know, or they’d make little comments right after I’d gotten some letter or call. It’s all connected, even if everybody wants to act like I’m “reading into it.”

I’ve been watching it for almost two years now. Papers don’t change what I’ve seen. They can print anything on letterhead and call it normal procedure, but that doesn’t mean there isn’t a plan behind it. So yes, I guess I do think people have been quietly working together, not just with the house, but around me, to push me out.

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
I mean… not usually, no. If it’s just a normal day, I can get myself up and go to work. I supervise my team, I deal with the schedule, customer complaints, people needing overrides, all of that. Retail doesn’t really let you just sit around deciding whether to start or not, you know?
